title: Chicken drumstick, baked or broiled, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken drumstick prepared by baking or broiling is a common item in fast‑food restaurants and casual dining. The skin stays on, providing flavor, moisture and a crispy texture. It is usually served hot, often with sauces or side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks contain more fat than breast meat, making them juicier and more flavorful.
When baked, the skin forms a golden crust that locks in moisture.
In the United States the term "drumsticks" is widely used for this cut, especially in kids' meals.
Asian cuisines often marinate drumsticks in soy sauce, honey and spices before grilling.
Drumsticks are a staple of barbecue menus, glazed with sweet‑tangy sauces and cooked low and slow.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from meat helps maintain hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: The skin contains collagen, which may benefit skin and joint health.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Drumsticks are fattier than breast meat, so they should be limited in low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sodium in prepared dishes
items.content: Fast‑food versions often come with salty sauces that can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked drumsticks may harbor salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Chicken protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drumsticks are typically eaten hot, pulling the meat off the bone. The crispy skin can be eaten as is or dipped in sauces. They pair well with fries, salads, or barbecue sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh drumsticks keep in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen, they last up to 6 months at –18 °C. Thaw frozen pieces in the fridge before cooking, and store cooked drumsticks in an airtight container for no more than 3 days.
